reader_question: When did states set their minimum wage above the federal $7.25?
grade_line: Documented: the Department of Labor’s table of state minimum wages on January 1 of each year shown
title: Thirty states and DC had a minimum wage above the federal $7.25 on January 1, 2024, up from 14 states and DC on January 1, 2010.
measure_line: Each state’s basic minimum wage under state law for non-farm work, against the federal $7.25, on January 1 of 2010, 2014, 2019 and 2024, 50 states and the District of Columbia, in three classes.
notes: On July 1, 2026, 30 states and DC set a minimum wage above $7.25, 13 states set $7.25, Georgia and Wyoming set $5.15, and five states had no minimum wage law, so the federal rate applies there to covered employers, by the count in our systems atlas, Who Do They Answer To? (claim CL1516, graded documented, from the Department of Labor’s state minimum wage page of that date; atlas snapshot of October 15, 2026).
Classes follow each state’s highest listed rate, and some rates apply only to larger employers. Where a state’s rate is below $7.25, or it has none, employers the federal law covers pay $7.25.

The map draws Alaska and Hawaii apart and not to scale, and the District of Columbia as a square beside Maryland. The Department’s table also lists Guam, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, which the map does not draw.

The table gives each state’s rate at each date as the Department prints it, with “No state law” where a state has none. In it, [c], (d) and (e) mark rates for employers of four, six or two or more workers, and (g) marks a state that sets a lower rate for some smaller businesses.
source_line: Source: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, Changes in Basic Minimum Wages in Non-Farm Employment Under State Law, January 1 rates in 2010, 2014, 2019 and 2024, 50 states and DC; U.S. Census Bureau, Cartographic Boundary Files, 2024, states. Retrieved November 12 and 13, 2026. Classes by Oath & Action from each state’s highest listed rate; some rates apply only to larger employers, and where a state is below $7.25 or has none, covered employers pay the federal rate.
alt: Four maps of the states on January 1 of 2010, 2014, 2019 and 2024, each state shaded by whether its minimum wage was above the federal $7.25, at it, or below it or absent. States above $7.25 grew from 14 and DC in 2010 to 23 and DC in 2014, 29 and DC in 2019 and 30 and DC in 2024, spreading from the coasts and the Northeast into the Midwest; most of the South stayed at $7.25 or had no state minimum.
